clue.text: It might do one credit to be so obscure

indicators.note: to do something over is to rework it, so these letters are to be reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A remark that being abstruse earns a person some credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might do' is the anagram signal working on ONE CREDIT; 'It' and 'to be so' are link words. The surface's 'do one credit' sounds like praise, but the words are only raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite knowledge is little known and hard to grasp, a synonym of obscure.

clue.text: And jam roll at dance sessions-?

definitions.text: And jam roll at dance sessions-?

parts.words: And jam roll at dance sessions-?
parts.note: a jam roll is a cake, and rock is a dance, so cakes served at rock sessions would sit beside it

explanation.surface: Another treat served at dances, like the jam roll.
explanation.walkthrough: Jam roll, rock and roll, and jam session all suggest music; the answer is a small rough-topped bun named after a dance style.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hard fruit buns with craggy tops take their name from rocks, which here is read as the dance.

clue.text: The Frenchman in the fiacre came to the Promised Land

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person who did this

indicators.note: the French article goes inside the vehicle, as passengers sit in a cab

parts.note: a fiacre is a French horse-drawn cab
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A Frenchman rides in a cab to reach Canaan.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of a man: one of the spies sent by Moses, and with Joshua the only adult of the Exodus to enter Canaan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Numbers, this spy was one of two adults of the Exodus allowed to enter Canaan.

clue.text: Two passages in the central feature

definitions.text: Two passages in the central feature

parts.words: Two passages in the central feature
parts.note: the central feature of a face is the nose, which holds two air passages

explanation.surface: Two corridors at the heart of a building's design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central feature' sounds architectural, but it is the nose in the middle of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The two openings of the nose are air passages in the face's central feature.

clue.text: Better that I am put to the test

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am
proved in its older sense means tested, as in 'the proof of the pudding'

explanation.surface: Being tested made me better.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made better has been enhanced or upgraded.

clue.text: No longer saucy to the specialist

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer so
pert means cheeky or saucy

explanation.surface: A formerly cheeky pupil now defers to the specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist is an authority with skill in a field.

clue.text: Drudge at home for a villainous master

parts.note: a fag is a drudge, a schoolboy made to serve an older pupil
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A servant stays home while working for a wicked employer.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag, in British public-school slang, is a junior boy who runs errands for a senior: a drudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Oliver Twist has a criminal who trains and commands a gang of boy pickpockets.

clue.text: Omar's writing apparatus

parts.note: in FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam, 'The Moving --- writes; and, having writ, moves on'

explanation.surface: The pen used by a Persian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous quatrain is 'The Moving Finger writes; and, having writ, Moves on'; the writing tool is part of a hand, not a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Rubaiyat, a digit of the hand of fate does the writing.

clue.text: "Effingham, ——, Raleigh, Drake" (Newbolt)

parts.note: fill the gap in Newbolt's roll-call of Elizabethan sea captains, in his poem The Fighting Temeraire

explanation.surface: A roll of Elizabethan seamen with one name missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Newbolt's 'Admirals All' lists 'Effingham, Grenville, Raleigh, Drake'; Sir Richard Grenville died commanding the Revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing name is the Elizabethan captain of the Revenge, who fought a Spanish fleet off the Azores.

clue.text: Two points about a single date

indicators.note: the two compass letters go around the other piece, as about means surrounding

parts.note: N and S are two points of the compass, north and south
a single means one

explanation.surface: Two people meet for a one-off date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ONE inside N and S. The date is from the Roman calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar this was the ninth day before the Ides, a fixed day of the month.

clue.text: Summons in a colourful way

parts.note: a military summons calls recruits to the colours, the regimental flags, so the summons is colourful in that sense

explanation.surface: A vivid, flamboyant way of issuing a summons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colourful' looks like flamboyant, but the colours are a regiment's flags, and being summoned to them means conscription.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscription orders draft people into the armed forces, joining the regiment's flags.

clue.text: Divinely rural types of pipes

parts.note: the pipes belong to the Greek god of shepherds and the countryside, so they are both divine and rustic

explanation.surface: Pipes with a heavenly countryside air.
explanation.definitionFit: Panpipes are named after the goat-footed Greek god of flocks, who played reed pipes in the wild.

clue.text: It's thrown up in a brace of shakes

definitions.text: It's thrown up in a brace of shakes

parts.words: It's thrown up in a brace of shakes
parts.note: a brace of shakes means very quickly, but here the thing is a heavy pole tossed into the air at Highland games

explanation.surface: Something tossed into the air in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing the pole is a Scottish Highland games event: a long tree trunk is heaved upward so it turns end over end.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk thrown at Highland games is tossed up and over in a single heave.

clue.text: We 'turn sour on the little folk

indicators.note: placed on means written after the other piece
to turn milk is to sour it, but here the word means the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: elves are the little folk of folklore

explanation.surface: We grow bitter towards the fairies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like part of 'turn sour' (go bad), but it is the anagram signal on the next word; 'on' places the little folk after it. 'We' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive first-person plural pronoun stands for the speakers themselves, as 'we' does.

clue.text: "Ring in … The larger heart, the —— hand" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: "Ring in … The larger heart, the —— hand" (Tennyson)

parts.words: "Ring in … The larger heart, the —— hand" (Tennyson)
parts.note: fill the gap in Tennyson's New Year poem, where the bells ring in a more generous heart and a gentler hand

explanation.surface: A line of Tennyson with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from In Memoriam's 'Ring out, wild bells': 'Ring in the valiant man and free, The larger heart, the kindlier hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the comparative of a word meaning gentle and generous, fitting a larger heart.

clue.text: No bird. Edward, yet put up for election

parts.note: mina is a variant spelling of myna, the Asian starling
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: No candidate yet: Edward has not been put forward to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet' is a link word. MINA is an old spelling of the myna bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate put forward to stand has been proposed for the post.

clue.text: Dull apartment

definitions.meaning: a set of rooms on one floor

explanation.definitionFit: A dull voice or drink lacks sparkle; British English calls an apartment by the same word.

clue.text: Mates wrestling in a marquee with a will

indicators.note: the shuffled friends are placed inside the marquee, as wrestlers in a tent

parts.note: a marquee is a large tent

indicators.note: wrestling bodies twist about, so the letters of the word mates are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Friends wrestle in a big tent with great determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrestling' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container signal; 'with a' is a link. 'will' looks like determination in the surface but is the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will is the legal document setting out what a person leaves when they die.

clue.text: A vowel change would make this country a capital district

definitions.text: A vowel change would make this country a capital district

parts.words: A vowel change would make this country a capital district
parts.note: swap one vowel in the name of a South American country and you get the US federal district holding Washington

explanation.surface: A country whose name differs by one vowel from a national capital district.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the O after L to a U and the country becomes the District of Columbia.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American republic named after Columbus differs by one vowel from the US capital's district.

clue.text: Spotted just a little bit in front

parts.note: a speck is a tiny bit
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: Seen ahead by only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' is a link word. 'Spotted' looks like 'seen', but it means dotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with small dots or flecks, like a bird's egg.

clue.text: Amounts that make us turn to writing

indicators.note: to make the word us turn is to read it the other way round

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Figures that send us off to put pen to paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' turns US into SU; 'to writing' adds MS, a manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Totals of money or figures are amounts added together.

clue.text: Parsons at weddings found in the organ-loft?

definitions.meaning: clergy who join bride and groom as a pair
an organ has mechanisms linking one keyboard to another, found up in the loft

explanation.surface: Clergymen at a wedding hiding up near the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson pairs off two people in marriage; an organ's linking stops join manuals or pedals together.

clue.text: Go briskly into a quarrel ?

definitions.meaning: to move along easily and fast
an old British colloquial word for a row or squabble

explanation.surface: Stepping quickly straight into an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail through is to move with brisk ease; in old British slang the same word meant a row or tiff.

clue.text: Canons to right of them. Canons to left of them ?

definitions.text: Canons to right of them. Canons to left of them ?

parts.words: Canons to right of them. Canons to left of them ?
parts.note: echoes Tennyson's 'Cannon to right of them' but means clergy living in the enclosed precincts of a cathedral

explanation.surface: Tennyson's guns, misspelt as clergymen, all around.
explanation.walkthrough: The line recalls 'The Charge of the Light Brigade', but the canons are clergy, who live around a cathedral's enclosed precinct.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathedral precincts, where the clergy of the chapter live, are enclosed grounds named after being shut in.

clue.text: "Sweet and Low" her forte?

parts.note: Sweet and Low is a Victorian song, and a low female singing voice is the one to sing it

explanation.surface: A singer whose specialty is a gentle lullaby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forte' is the musical word for loud but also means a strong point; the song 'Sweet and Low' suits the lowest female voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest female singing voice suits a song marked low.

clue.text: Hoods for many night-birds

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
owls are birds of the night

explanation.surface: Hoods for flocks of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks wear loose hooded garments over the head.

clue.text: Mark of division among lepidopterists

parts.note: a punctuation mark that divides a sentence, which is also the name of a butterfly with a white mark on its wing

explanation.surface: A rift among butterfly collectors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'division' suggests a quarrel among collectors; the mark is punctuation, and butterfly experts know a species by the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark separating clauses shares its name with an orange butterfly bearing a white C-shaped mark.

clue.text: "We loathe our —— and we long for quails" (Dryden)

definitions.text: We loathe our —— and we long for quails" (Dryden)

parts.words: We loathe our —— and we long for quails" (Dryden)
parts.note: fill the gap in Dryden's line from Absalom and Achitophel, recalling the Israelites tiring of the food sent from heaven

explanation.surface: A line of Dryden with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dryden recalls Numbers 11, where the Israelites grew sick of the food sent from heaven and craved meat; God then sent quails.
explanation.definitionFit: The bread from heaven fed Israel in the wilderness, until they tired of it and asked for quails.

clue.text: Seer in the box

parts.note: not a prophet but someone who saw an event and now stands in the courtroom box to testify

explanation.surface: A prophet shut in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seer' wants to be a prophet; here it is literally one who saw, giving evidence from the courtroom box.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who saw a crime gives evidence from the stand in court.

clue.text: The rest is in the hand of justice

definitions.meaning: the remainder, what is left over
the statue of Justice holds a pair of scales

explanation.surface: Leisure is in the hands of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: What remains of an account is its remainder; Justice's scales are the weighing device she holds.

clue.text: There's a warbler in the south border

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A songbird is spotted along the southern boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the bird's full name: the 'sedge warbler' is a common reed-bed songbird, called by its first word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown marsh songbird is named after the grassy plant it nests among.

clue.text: Hold it, Mister !

definitions.meaning: to stand firm, not give way
A pilgrim in Bunyan's allegory and the title of a John Buchan novel

explanation.surface: Wait a moment, sir!
explanation.definitionFit: To hold one's ground is to stay firm; the title character of Buchan's novel is a Mister of that name.
